output.summary: A flowering tree native to the Pacific Coast and adjacent highlands of Mexico, Central America and northern South America, Madras thorn has a spiny trunk and fragrant greenish-white flowers. Its ripe pods turn pink and split open to reveal pink or white pulp, which is eaten raw in several countries and used in drinks.
output.edibilityNote: Sweet-and-sour pod pulp is eaten raw, served with meat dishes, or mixed with sugar and water for drinks.
